I added the tree search, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec: the "tree search" test and the three longer scenarios.

There's now a search box and button on the main screen. Pressing the button lists every person on this sheet and the other sheets in its tree whose name or an alias contains the typed text, case ignored. Each line reads `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people, by sheet id. A blank search lists everyone. The result count is cleared while a search runs, and a failed search shows an error.

- **Server:** a new read-only endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/search?text=…`, in `TreeSearchController.java` and `TreeSearchService.java` under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/search/`. It finds the tree with the existing `SheetRepository.tree` (all ancestors and all their descendants). The due-totals come from the existing `Rollup.take`, so they match the figures shown on each sheet, with `n/a` when a person has none. It writes nothing to the store or the audit file.
- **Front end:** a service in `core/search.ts` and a panel in `features/search/search.ts`, built the same way as the audit viewer. The panel sits on the home screen after the summary.

Three behaviours the request didn't specify, so I chose them:
- Retired people are always included, whether or not "show retired" is on. The test only searches with it on.
- The search ignores the "as of" date and always uses current figures.
- Spaces at either end of the typed text are dropped before matching.

No database changes were needed.
